picks.title: Roblox announce plans to let people AI-generate basic games using text prompts in a mobile app, but claim it won't fill their homepage with AI slop
picks.headline: Roblox announce plans to let people AI-generate basic games using text prompts in a mobile app, but claim it won't fill their homepage with AI slop
picks.excerpt: Roblox has unveiled 'Build', a mobile app that lets anyone generate a basic playable game from natural-language text prompts, part of a push to lower the barrier to creation on the platform. The company insists the AI-generated experiences won't flood its homepage with low-effort 'slop', framing the tool as an on-ramp for new creators rather than a replacement for its established Studio pipeline. It's a notable text-to-game milestone from one of the biggest UGC platforms, raising fresh questions about discoverability and quality control.
picks.rationale: Text-to-game from a major UGC platform is a concrete new capability that changes how solo/new creators prototype — high novelty, high actionability, reputable outlet.

picks.title: How do you feel about AI videogame music?
picks.headline: How do you feel about AI videogame music?
picks.excerpt: PC Gamer opens a discussion on the growing use of generative AI to compose and produce game soundtracks, asking whether game music still requires 'the human touch'. The piece weighs the creative and craft implications for composers and audio designers as AI music tools become cheap and capable enough to score games, and gathers reader sentiment on where AI-generated scores cross the line for players.
picks.rationale: Directly relevant to audio designers/composers weighing generative music tools in game pipelines; freshest item in the pool (07-26) and a distinct craft angle from the visual-asset stories.

picks.title: Poll finds 100% of Japanese online game developers are using AI, though mostly for user preference analysis and user behavior prediction
picks.headline: Poll finds 100% of Japanese online game developers are using AI, though mostly for user preference analysis and user behavior prediction
picks.excerpt: A survey from Japan's Online Game Association finds that every polled Japanese online-game developer now uses AI in some form, though adoption skews toward analytics - user-preference analysis and player-behavior prediction - rather than generative content creation. The data offers a rare, concrete snapshot of how a major games market is actually integrating AI into development and live-ops workflows, and where studios are (and aren't) yet trusting it in the creative pipeline.
picks.rationale: A hard adoption data point on where AI is (and isn't) trusted in a major games market — informs how teams position AI in dev/live-ops workflows; credible survey, distinct from creative-tool releases.
